findings_scoring.title: The numerator scopes on ONE org axis while the denominator admits TWO -- silent 0.0% for the mismatched axis
findings_scoring.detail: UniqueLprCaseClaimsQuery.php:251 `AND ({org} = 0 OR hotlist_org_id = {org})`. The denominator (kept, :209) admits a claim on EITHER side: forwarder_org_id = ? OR agent_org_id = ?. hits_cold.hotlist_org_id is the single order-owning org and can equal at most one of them. So for every claim where forwarder != agent, exactly one participating org gets zero numerator credit while still carrying the claim in its denominator -> the card renders 0.0%, which is ALSO the legitimate no-claims reading, so a wrong answer is indistinguishable from a right one behind a 24h cache.
findings_scoring.why_it_is_mine: The driver ADDED this predicate for Q5's 9.7% prune win. Worse, the driver wrote into measure-rate-card.sql that it 'is also wanted for tenant correctness' -- all three lanes independently PROVED that false: h is already narrowed by `hotlist_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT hotlist_id FROM oc)` and oc descends from the already org-filtered kept, so the predicate buys ZERO isolation. It is a pure optimisation with a correctness cost.
findings_scoring.aggravating: Lane 3: the pre-claim population is BY DEFINITION pre-assignment sightings = Staging hits, and the repo documents hotlist_org_id as exactly the axis that silently drops them -- StagingLiveHitLeaderQuery:20-22, okf/concepts/scout-dashboard-stats.md:19-21, okf/concepts/scout-birds-eye.md:92, ClarityScoutMapController:298, ClarityScoutBirdsEyeController:712/969, okf/concepts/missed-opportunity.md:27-35 ('Getting this backwards is the classic missed-opportunity bug'). Also: the driver's Q5 measurement covered ONE org of 257 and never recorded which axis it sat on.

findings_scoring.title: The sibling's documented MIN_TTL_SECONDS floor was dropped, and windowRate() has no cold-path lock at all
findings_scoring.detail: UniqueLprCaseClaims floors getCacheTTL() at 60s with a load-bearing comment: getCacheTTL() collapses to 10s under admin_impersonator, shorter than the query's contended p99 (9.3s), so a re-render starts the next ~40M-row scan before the previous returns. UniqueScansToCaseClaims copies COLD_BLOCK_SECONDS/COLD_LOCK_SECONDS/REFRESH_LOCK_SECONDS verbatim but omits the floor -- on a query that is 3-5x heavier. windowRate() also uses a bare cache()->remember() with no heldFlexible lock, so N tabs on a cold key = N concurrent multi-GB scans. The card's own comment claiming 'same measured p99 query shape' is false.
findings_scoring.fix: Add the getCacheTTL() floor override; route windowRate() through heldFlexible(); correct the false p99 comment.

findings_scoring.title: The org-scoped query path -- the ONLY path production renders -- has zero test coverage
findings_scoring.detail: All seven query tests pass null as $orgId -> {org}=0 -> BOTH org predicates constant-fold to true. Every widget test stubs fetchWindowTotal/fetchMonthlySeries, so no org id reaches SQL either. Deleting line 251 changes no test result -- the H1 mutation survives the entire suite. seedHit() also hardcodes hotlist_org_id = 1 with no modelled relationship to the claim's forwarder or agent.
findings_scoring.fix: Add org-scoped tests, including the H1 scenario (agent-side claim whose hotlist_org_id is the forwarder) asserting the org still gets numerator credit.

findings_scoring.title: clarity.hits_cold read without FINAL on a two-argument ReplacingMergeTree
findings_scoring.detail: hits_cold is ReplacingMergeTree(_version, _peerdb_is_deleted) -- the TWO-arg form, where FINAL does drop tombstones (contrast PG-028's one-arg billing_events case). With _peerdb_is_deleted = 0 alone, a soft-deleted-but-unmerged hit still has its earlier version physically present and contributes to min(scanned_at), so a deleted pre-claim sighting still flips pre_claim true. Error direction is one-way: it can only inflate. The class spends 25 lines justifying FINAL on orgs then departs from that rule for a second table with no recorded argument.
findings_scoring.fix: Add FINAL to the hits_cold read.

residual_findings.title: COLD_BLOCK_SECONDS = 12 is sized against a different, lighter query's p99, and the shipped shape has never been measured

Lane 1 also notes clarity_clickhouse sets no max_execution_time, so a timed-out waiter abandons the HTTP request while ClickHouse keeps executing.

residual_findings.title: FINAL on hits_cold rests on a premise the ticket's own prep measured as false, and is now proven answer-neutral
residual_findings.detail: The aggregate is min(), which is duplicate-idempotent, so RMT non-dedup cannot change the answer; the tombstone row itself is already excluded by _peerdb_is_deleted = 0. And FINAL cannot dedup this table anyway: hit_created_at is mutable and sits in BOTH the sort key and the partition key, so a mutated version and its predecessor coexist under FINAL -- which is exactly what AC-3's own reason in prep-context records. Meanwhile optimize_move_to_prewhere_if_final defaults to 0, so FINAL suppresses PREWHERE movement for the hotlist_id IN (...) filter and forces merge-on-read across 247 partitions. THE DRIVER'S RE-MEASUREMENT CONFIRMS IT: 11,573 with FINAL, 11,573 without. Pure unmeasured cost for zero measured benefit.

residual_findings.title: windowRate() passes [$ttl, $ttl] where $ttl is an ABSOLUTE instant, halving the fresh window repeatedly
residual_findings.detail: Cache::flexible tests freshness as created + getSeconds($ttl[0]) > now(), and getSeconds() on a DateTimeInterface returns the remainder measured AT READ TIME. With an absolute instant the entry is fresh only while T < T0 + D/2, then every render serves stale AND defer()s a refresh that re-executes the multi-GB query; each refresh resets created but reuses the original absolute instant, so freshness halves again (T0+300, +450, +525...). Roughly 4-6 extra full scans per org per 10-minute cycle, ~30 while impersonating at the 60s floor. Those refreshes take the warm path, so the cold lock does not guard them. Introduced by RN1 fix #3: the monthly seam is correct ([3600, 86400], plain integers) and the sibling's window path uses cache()->remember(), for which an absolute instant IS correct. Invisible to the round-trip test, which reads back within milliseconds.

residual_findings.title: Should the numerator count only the viewing org's OWN cameras (kit_org_id) rather than any Insight camera?

Lane 2 examined the same code and CLEARED it as not a tenancy break -- h is narrowed by hotlist_id IN (SELECT ... FROM oc), oc is a subset of kept, and kept carries the org predicate, so only the viewing org's own claims are reachable and the output is one boolean folded into a count; no other tenant's row content is exposed. Lane 2 further notes that adding kit_org_id = {org} would COLLAPSE the card for most orgs and break the 96.6% reproduction. The metric's approved wording is '96.6% of claimed vehicles were seen by OUR cameras first', and in DEV-2409 comment 39126 'our' means INSIGHT's network -- the fleet-wide figure AC-1 pins has no kit_org_id filter. This is a genuine product-semantics fork, not a defect both lanes agree on. NOT auto-answered (non-negotiable 1).

(b) min() is duplicate-idempotent only if scanned_at is immutable across CDC versions; hits_cold carries _peerdb_scan_synced_at DEFAULT toDateTime('1970-01-01'), so a row synced before its scan facet lands has scanned_at at the 1970 column default -- min() then returns 1970, which precedes every claim. That is the SAME 1970 failure mode the h.hotlist_id != 0 guard exists for, arriving through a door the guard cannot cover (the join genuinely matches).
residual_findings.fix: The DECISION (remove FINAL) was operator-sanctioned and measured answer-neutral; keep it. Correct the recorded REASON, and add `AND scanned_at > toDateTime(0)` to close the 1970-default path (one line, unconditionally safe -- a 1970 scan is not a real sighting).

residual_findings.title: Peak memory x concurrency at the documented 29-org cardinality is still unmeasured
residual_findings.detail: h aggregates all 26.0M hits_cold rows into an un-spillable LEFT JOIN build side (max_bytes_in_join and join_algorithm are unset on clarity_clickhouse; max_bytes_before_external_group_by bounds only the GROUP BY). Cold locks are keyed per (card, date, org) so they never serialise across orgs, and getMonthlyData()'s key embeds Y-m so EVERY entitled org's key rotates simultaneously at each UTC month boundary -- in addition to every deploy/cache:clear. 29 orgs x ~930 MiB = ~27 GB, or ~54 GB if the window seam is cold too. residual_findings.lanes: 1/3 (lane 1) -- SELF-INFLICTED BY THE RN3 S6 FIX
residual_findings.title: My S6 'correction' replaced a CORRECT mechanism account with a false one
residual_findings.detail: Lane 1 verified against Illuminate\Cache\Repository (:622-662, :810-821) with concrete arithmetic. With the pre-fix [$abs,$abs]: putMany uses getSeconds($ttl[1]) = ~600, so hard expiry is created+600 -- NOT 'the same instant' as the new comment claims. Freshness is created + getSeconds($ttl[0]) > now(), and getSeconds() re-measures a DateTimeInterface AT READ TIME, so at offset d it is fresh iff 600-d > d, i.e. d < 300. So for 300 <= d < 600 the entry was present-but-stale and defer() DID run. The deferred branch was REACHABLE and the original RN3 lane-3 'halving' account was RIGHT. I instructed the worker that the real defect was $ttl[1] === $ttl[0] making the branch unreachable; that is false, and it now ships in app code while the CORRECT account survives in the herd-guard test -- two comments in one change giving mutually exclusive mechanisms.
residual_findings.fix: Restore the halving account (fresh window collapses to D/2 and re-halves on each deferred refresh) in the widget docblock; reconcile with the test comment.

residual_findings.lanes: 1/3 (lane 1) -- SELF-INFLICTED BY THE RN2 R5 FIX, user-visible
residual_findings.title: 'Today' can serve the PREVIOUS local day's rate for ~40 minutes after midnight, and my R5 fix quadrupled the exposure
residual_findings.detail: windowRate()'s key is buildWidgetCacheKey('today', $orgId) -- NO day component -- and windowTtlSeconds() now returns [600, 2400]. Cached at 23:55 local, hard expiry is 00:35 the next day. At 00:20 both keys are present, the freshness test fails, so Cache::flexible defers a refresh and RETURNS THE STALE VALUE: yesterday's full-day rate rendered as this morning's 'Today'. Every sibling card is bounded at 10 minutes because DashboardWidget::currentPeriodTotal() uses cache()->remember() with an absolute 600s expiry and no serve-stale branch. The pre-R5 [$abs,$abs] pair hard-expired at created+600, so MY R5 REPAIR QUADRUPLED THIS on a day-scoped key. getMonthlyData() gets it right (its key carries Y-m) and UniqueLprCaseClaims documents at length that 'the key MUST carry the window's identity'.
residual_findings.fix: Add a day component to the window key (NOT a shorter hard TTL -- that trades directly against the cold-miss envelope).

residual_findings.title: oc.hotlist_id != 0 is dead code, its comment claims it is load-bearing, and the S5(a) test written to pin it is vacuous
residual_findings.detail: All three lanes proved it independently, two by mutating the rendered SQL against a live ClickHouse fixture including a hostile hotlist_id=0 hit. S4's restored prune (hotlist_id IN (SELECT ... FROM oc WHERE hotlist_id != 0)) means h can never hold a hotlist-0 row, so the join always misses and h.hotlist_id != 0 rejects it alone. Deleting oc.hotlist_id != 0 leaves the entire suite green. Same defect class as the vacuous test S5(c) repaired -- reintroduced by S5(a) in the same commit. Lane 1's mutation table also confirms h.hotlist_id != 0 and scanned_at > toDateTime(0) ARE genuinely load-bearing, and that S4's prune is answer-neutral as documented.
residual_findings.fix: Either drop WHERE hotlist_id != 0 from the IN subquery so the conjunct becomes load-bearing and bind the test to it, or delete the conjunct and the coverage claim in both the SQL comment and the test docblock.

residual_findings.title: The two guard-constant docblocks cite the pre-RN3 shape's measurements as this shape's
residual_findings.detail: They state 106.8M read_rows / 3,828 MiB / 5.1s uncontended. The shipped shape measures 107,321,250 / 3,864.1 MiB / 1,035 ms -- a 5x difference in wall time. The 4-way contended run was also of the earlier heavier shape. Qualitative conclusions hold (12s still clears 6.4s), but the record is wrong -- and the single most decision-relevant number, the 235.0 MiB peak driving the ~6.7 GB projection, appears only in the query class, not in the widget an engineer reads when re-sizing these constants.

residual_findings.title: The epoch-0 guard's stated mechanism is a non-sequitur
residual_findings.detail: The comment attributes scanned_at's 1970 value to _peerdb_scan_synced_at's explicit DEFAULT toDateTime('1970-01-01'). A default on one column does not populate another. The real mechanism is ClickHouse's implicit zero for a non-Nullable DateTime omitted from an INSERT. This matters for a future reader: toDateTime('1970-01-01') is parsed in the SERVER timezone, so anyone 'correcting' the guard to match the quoted default would make it timezone-dependent. The guard as written (> toDateTime(0)) is correct and mutation-verified; only the reason is wrong.

residual_findings.title: Remaining low-severity items
residual_findings.detail: (a) No differential test pins that the re-derived deduped equals the shipped deduped -- the substance of AC-2. Two lanes verified the equality empirically across adversarial fixtures (blank VIN, failed claim, absent hotlist_id, insightlpr forwarder, cross-month, both org axes) and it holds; nothing keeps it holding. (b) The e2e test TITLE still names 'LPR Repossessions' though the assertions and docblock were corrected -- it is what CI prints on failure. (c) ~70 lines of herd-guard machinery duplicated from the sibling, and the copy dropped the sibling's rationale that both flexible keys must be checked because they land in different prod-Redis-cluster slots -- exactly the counter-evidence a future 'this looks redundant' simplification should trip over. (d) DashboardMetricCard's docblock now says 3 overriders of 7 cards; it is 5 of 16.

rn4_fixes_applied.T2: windowRate()'s cache key now carries the VIEWER-LOCAL DAY ($this->date.':'.now(tz: $timezone)->toDateString()). Because windowTtlSeconds() returns [600, 2400], a value cached at 23:55 local previously outlived its fresh window and Cache::flexible served it at 00:20 as the new day's 'Today' -- yesterday's full-day rate. PINNED by a new behavioural test (test_today_is_recomputed_after_the_viewer_local_midnight_not_served_stale) plus a new ScanCasesWindowCountingWidget double, and MUTATION-VERIFIED: reverting the key change makes it fail. This is the second vacuous test I have written on this ticket; mutation-testing every guard fix is what caught both.
rn4_fixes_applied.T3: Resolved by option (b): DELETED the redundant `oc.hotlist_id != 0` conjunct. My first attempt was option (a) -- drop `WHERE hotlist_id != 0` from the prune so the conjunct became load-bearing -- and MUTATION PROVED IT WRONG: the join is an equality on hotlist_id, so even a real hits_cold row with hotlist_id = 0 matching 0 => 0 still yields h.hotlist_id = 0, which h.hotlist_id != 0 rejects. The conjunct is redundant UNCONDITIONALLY, for any data; option (a) was never achievable. The prune filter was restored, the conjunct removed, and both comments rewritten to state that h.hotlist_id != 0 is sufficient on its own and why. Mutation-verified: removing h.hotlist_id != 0 now fails TWO tests.
rn4_fixes_applied.T1: windowTtlSeconds()'s docblock restored to the TRUE mechanism. driver_verified_findings.consequence: A rate card must compute its float end-to-end inside getCardRate() (the stub's own new seam, UniqueScansToCaseClaims.php:45) and must NOT route today/last_7d through currentPeriodTotal()/getRangeTotal()/getModelQueryForDates() -- all of which return int and would TRUNCATE the rate to 0 or 1.
